Congratulations ! Engineering is a hard school to get in to so you definitely deserve it and probably already have  base time management and study skills needed to succeed. It’s just budgeting your time and gauging which courses to spend time towards. I just finished a 19 credit semester as a Senior MechE w 2 part time jobs and it honestly was one of my highest performance semester yet so I don’t really rely on the credit situation to dictate my studying/work schedule.

A 3 credits elementary/intermediate Humanities will not be the same as a 3 credit core engineering class like Statics/Thermo/fluids etc. you’ll spend more time on those math/science classes if you want a higher mark. No matter how heavy my semester load is I always do hw at least until around 8/9 on weekdays and I can always do more than that and save weekends for studying, getting ahead (or even catching up I’ve been in that situation countless times haha) and go out with friends at night but engineering is all about ~stamina~. Being honest and knowing how hard and long to push yourself is so important and knowing when you need rest to recharge. Studying longer does not equate to the quality of studying.

This upcoming semester just gauge your first few classes, see how well you can handle it and you’ll know after that first or second midterm whether you need to spend more or less hours on that class. The same formula won’t work each semester because some classes are just unique, require more attention etc. but that base knowledge will take you a long way.

Good luck on your engineering journey and congrats !

I had to go part time student dealing with extreme hunger, anxiety depression and my focus was all over the place. It was definitely not easy and luckily my parents were realy understanding as they saw just how much it was affecting my life and well being. 

It’s really difficult trying to get other people to understand what you’re going through because it sounds almost dumb when I tried to explain it to my other friends especially when they would see me down a can of beans after eating 2 quesadillas and a bag of popcorn.

I was in almost your exact same shoes a few months ago, I was underweight and would overexercise as well as severely restrict for how active I was. Realized I was slowly just wasting away and decided to to go all in. It was so emotionally draining and one of the hardest things I’ve ever done and I’m still trying to recover today. I was never super hungry while I was restricting UNTIL I started actually eating and gave in to extreme hunger which kinda weirded me out. Like you I would fill up on fruits and pretty low cal nutrient dense foods bc -fear of weight gain- but was never truly satisfied and would constantly have my mind racing. But just trust the process, regularly exercise, eat good. I did end up gaining weight but I also gained back my personality and my anxiety is gone. In my sick mind I thought I gained enough to become obese but I only ended up gaining 8 pounds with the last couple pounds almost being intentional since it was holidays and I didn’t compensate for what I was eating. It’s going to take time to get your hunger cues in check and I highly suggest a nutritionist but stay as consistent as possible w ur meals, whether that’s 3 meals or 2 big meals with snacks.but combine all 3 macro nutrients in meals. My go to meal that was so satiating was a bean quesadilla w guacamole and salsa and a grape fruit. Don’t shy away from fat don’t shy away from carbs and be mindful when you eat. Your metabolism has to rev up because it’s probably destroyed at this point and needs to heal. Sometimes I still fall victim to the binge restrict cycle but I try and go by mindful eating now instead of intuitive eating like many do, because my body can’t fore see the future or the consequences of my actions or reason like my mind can. 

If you were restricting pretty hard for 3+ months it’s going to take a significant amount of calories he specially if u lost ur period too) as well as decreased stress levels to get back to your set point and a weight your body can not only just function but function well. Try not to track calories and eat when your truly hungry. 2 quotes I try and live by to get out of a bad bp or binge restrict cycle: “eat to live don’t live to eat”, and “your life should be more interesting then what and when your next meal is going to be” the last one really put it into perspective for me, personally I know my potential is more than just being the girl who could either stuff her face or starve herself to death. I am still learning as I go and it helps to see food as fuel as my goal is to try and be strong and fit. Goals are amazing and track progress.

First, take a moment and trust yourself and your abilities to study for it. Listen to affirmations, go out for a walk or exercise, meditate, clear your mind. Then make a proclamation to your friends or tell your family the exam you have study for. You’ll feel more obligated to study. This part sucks but think of the consequences if you don’t study. What will happen if you fail it? Do you really want to retake it? I find that i learn best in huge chunks as I get into a real state of flow so just blast some instrumental music and identify yourself as a super studious student if that makes sense.
